follow-up time: Throughout pregnancy, delivery, and early childhood development (exact duration not specified)
cohort: Pregnant women with epilepsy (n=318) enrolled in the Taiwanese Registry of Epilepsy and Pregnancy (TREP) between 2004 and 2015
finding: While cesarean section rates were higher than usual in pregnant women with epilepsy, malformation rates remained low, and both outcomes were associated with obstetric complications but not AED risk factors.
mod_finding: Cesarean section rates were higher than usual in the study cohort.
